To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a bi-layer spin-on temporary bonding system has been developed that can be used to bond 200 mm and even 300 mm wafer pairs at room temperature with low cost, high throughput and high reliability.

the spin coated bi-layer TBS provides the following advantages: (1) low cost, (2) no need for specialized equipment to pretreat the wafers, (3) low TTV, (4) room temperature debonding and (5) high throughput.
we have developed a bi-layer spin-on temporary bonding film which enables the bonding and debonding of both 200 mm as well as 300 mm wavers in less than 15 min.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a low cost, room temperature, debondable spin on temporary bonding material which is a key enabler for the high volume manufacturing (HVM) of 2.3D ICs.
the development of an innovative low cost, room temperature, debondable spin on temporary bonding material for wafer level bonding and debonding of 300 mm diameter wafers for 2.25/3D IC applications.
the development and optimization of a bi-layer based temporary adhesive for the temporary bonding of 300 mm wavers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a low cost, room temperature, debondable spin on temporary bonding process which can be integrated with the current TSV processes and has the potential to significantly improve the throughput of 2.2D/3D stacking.
we have developed a low cost, room temperature, bi-layer spin on TBS that is compatible with both 200 and 300 mm wafer sizes.
the developed bi-layer based TBS is a low-cost, room temperature debonable spin-on temporary solution which can be easily implemented for 2. 5D/3 D IC packaging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current bi-layers spin-on temporary bonding solutions can be a key enabling technology for high volume manufacturing of stacked ICs.
the current TBS has been developed for high volume manufacturing of TSV based 2.5/3D stacking.
the current bi- layer spin on temporary bonding process is a key enabler for low cost, high throughput 2.5/3D ICs packaging.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a low cost, room temperature temporary bonding solution has been developed for 2. 5D/3 D IC stacking.
a simple spin-on TBS with a bi-layer structure can be used to achieve a high throughput temporary bonding process with a low TTV of bonded pairs.

a low cost, room temperature temporary bonding solution can be developed which can enable the high throughput of temporary bonding/debond processes and can also enable the high volume manufacturing (HVM) of 2. 5D/3DI stacking.
